incidents.vector: Voice-phishing / social engineering compromised cloud access; attackers re-entered after Instructure's May 2 'containment' by exploiting an issue tied to Free-For-Teacher accounts.
incidents.impact: Initial April 25 breach exfiltrated ~3.65 TB including names, emails, student IDs, and billions of private messages across ~9,000 K-12, university and corporate customers. Defacement on May 7 forced Instructure to take Canvas offline mid-final-exams, disrupting Princeton, Stanford, Columbia, UPenn, U. of Florida, Ohio State, NYC schools and many more; ransom deadline pushed to May 12.

incidents.victim: New York City Public Schools (Manhattan campus lab)
incidents.vector: Malware installed on shared computer-lab machines at one NYC public school site; vector and initial access path not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Malware was discovered and removed; NYPD and district investigators are probing alongside the separate Canvas outage hitting other NYC schools.

incidents.vector: Authenticated remote code execution via improper input validation (CVE-2026-6973) in Ivanti EPMM; likely chained from an earlier credential-theft step.
incidents.impact: Ivanti confirmed limited in-the-wild exploitation; CISA added the bug to the KEV catalog hours after disclosure. Four other high-severity EPMM defects were patched the same day. Earlier 2026 EPMM zero-days (CVE-2026-1281/1340) had spread to ~100 victims including Dutch government bodies.

incidents.vector: Microsoft Teams social-engineering (external chat, screen-share session that captured VPN credentials) and remote-management tooling, followed by Chaos ransomware-style extortion as a false-flag cover.
incidents.impact: Rapid7 confirmed espionage and data theft attributed to Iran's MOIS-linked MuddyWater group masquerading as a Chaos ransomware affiliate; victim data was published after no encryption occurred, and stolen files were verified legitimate.

incidents.vector: Two former employees retained or regained access to corporate systems after firing, then write-protected and deleted databases and obstructed the investigation.
incidents.impact: Sohaib Akhter convicted of deleting 96 government databases, password trafficking and accessing an EEOC complainant's email; the contractor served 45+ federal agencies. He faces up to 21 years in prison; sentencing September 9.

incidents.victim: DOD contractor / Schemata AI training platform
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated API exposed online without authentication on Schemata's virtual training platform.
incidents.impact: U.S. service-member records and sensitive military training course data were exposed; security firm Strix reported the leak took ~150 days to remediate.

incidents.victim: Polish municipal water-treatment facilities (Jabłonna Lacka, Szczytno, Małdyty, Tolkmicko, Sierakowo)
incidents.vector: Compromise of administrator accounts on plant industrial control systems, with attackers altering pump and alarm settings at one facility.
incidents.impact: Polish ABW intelligence service confirmed five water plants were breached in 2025; in some cases attackers could alter device parameters, posing direct risk to water-supply continuity. Disclosure is part of a wider warning about Russian-aligned sabotage and reconnaissance against Polish infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers (CL-STA-1132 victim)
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via buffer overflow (CVE-2026-0300) in PAN-OS User-ID Authentication / Captive Portal; attackers injected shellcode into nginx, enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account creds, and abused EarthWorm/ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 tracked limited but active exploitation by likely state-sponsored actors against PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, with disciplined log-wiping, multi-week residency and SAML-flood failover abuse to compromise paired devices. Exploitation began April 9 with successful RCE by mid-April.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Likely zero-day / n-day exploitation of internet-facing services, followed by Impacket reconnaissance, custom PowerShell scripts, AD Explorer snapshots, Chinese-language scanning tools (gogo, dddd) and deployment of NetDraft, CloudSorcerer, VSHELL/SNOWLIGHT and SNOWRUST malware.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos exposed a sophisticated China-nexus APT cluster (UAT-8302) targeting government bodies in South America since late 2024 and in southeastern Europe in 2025, sharing tooling with multiple Chinese-speaking espionage groups.

incidents.victim: Cloudflare, Vercel, Stripe and other Braintrust customers
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure, potentially reaching its API key database.
incidents.impact: AI observability startup Braintrust told customers to rotate API keys after attackers may have accessed its API key store; downstream exposure for major tech customers is being assessed.

incidents.vector: Authentication bypass (CVE-2026-41940) in cPanel/WHM allowing unauthenticated remote code execution; exposed control-panel interfaces are being targeted.
incidents.impact: ASD's ACSC issued a critical alert confirming active exploitation in Australia; the flaw affects all cPanel/WHM versions released since 2013, and CISA issued a parallel KEV warning.

incidents.victim: SAP CAP / npm developer ecosystem (@cap-js packages)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply chain (Mini Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP)
incidents.vector: Compromise of four widely used SAP Cloud Application Programming npm packages (@cap-js/sqlite, @cap-js/postgres, @cap-js/db-service, mbt) with malicious preinstall hooks running an obfuscated Bun-based credential stealer that exfiltrates GitHub/npm tokens and cloud secrets via GitHub commit dead-drops.
incidents.impact: Combined ~570K weekly downloads exposed; payload harvests AWS, Azure Key Vault, GCP, Kubernetes, Claude/MCP and crypto-wallet secrets, then self-propagates by republishing victim packages — extending the broader Shai-Hulud / @bitwarden/cli supply-chain wave.

incidents.victim: Delta Dental Insurance Company / Delta Dental of New York
incidents.vector: Exploitation of the mid-2023 MOVEit Transfer zero-day, with inadequate incident-response controls allowing attackers to exfiltrate large volumes of files.
incidents.impact: NYDFS imposed a $2.25M penalty and confirmed exfiltration of names, addresses, SSNs, driver's-license numbers, financial-account info and patient health information; the companies failed to notify DFS in time as required by 23 NYCRR Part 500.

incidents.vector: Compromise of AVB Disc Soft's website for nearly a month, with attackers swapping legitimate DAEMON Tools downloads for backdoored installers.
incidents.impact: Users who installed DAEMON Tools during the window received hidden backdoors; the vendor has now released clean versions and warned customers to reinstall.

incidents.victim: Cloud-hosted developer environments running TeamPCP / cloud secrets
incidents.vector: Modular Python worm scans Common Crawl parquet files for pre-validated targets, exploits exposed cloud services, and steals Kubernetes, Docker, SSH, GitHub, AWS, Slack, Outlook, Gmail, Mailchimp and crypto-wallet secrets while removing prior TeamPCP infections.
incidents.impact: SentinelLabs disclosed an active PCPJack campaign starting the week of April 20 that prioritizes credential and crypto-wallet theft over cryptomining and uniquely uses parquet-file target discovery; the actor is suspected to be a former TeamPCP insider.

incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service flood targeting Chime's customer-facing infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Some customers filed a class-action lawsuit alleging service disruption from the DDoS; Chime says the attack was fended off but the case raises questions on resilience and customer notification.

incidents.victim: Government of Mexico (federal tax authority, INE, Mexico City civil registry, Monterrey water utility)
incidents.vector: Operators used Anthropic's Claude Code to autonomously generate exploitation tooling and step-by-step intrusion guidance, breaching at least nine government entities via web portals and stolen credentials; OT crossover at Monterrey's vNode gateway was blocked by a login screen.
incidents.impact: Gambit Security and Dragos documented the first verified AI-directed cyberattack campaign, exfiltrating millions of tax records, property records and procurement data; the AI-led OT pivot at the Monterrey water utility failed against password-spraying and segmentation, limiting damage to IT-side records.
